correctness.rationale: C_t=BA_t and [A_t,B]=tA_tQA_t give K=(t−s)BRQR, Qe_k=e_(k+1)/[(k+1)(k+2)]. This verifies injectivity, strict lower triangularity and compactness; the triangular eigen-equation gives spectrum {0}. The leading D₃φ(S) has φ=z/[(1−tz)²(1−sz)²]; subtracting the frozen matrix formula replaces the inner weight by its difference from (n+1)⁻². For j≥n/2 the difference is O((n−j+1)/(n+1)³); for j<n/2 exponential convolution absorbs the powers. Thus the Schur-bounded residual has singular values O(n⁻⁴). The weighted-Toeplitz lemma follows by discarding O(δL) head rank and tail norm ≤ηλ, freezing the weights on blocks of length about √L for L=λ⁻¹ᐟᵞ, and using the finite Toeplitz trace moments. Threshold atoms do not affect the integrated limit since equality at a positive threshold has zero product measure in block position and angle. Analytic-symbol approximation is controlled in the weak ideal using the diagonal. Perturbation and inversion give exactly the stated circle mean cubed, Schatten statements, trace zero and logarithmic mean. At one zero parameter the binomial expansion gives the hypergeometric expression. Frozen finite checks were inspected but not executed; they do not certify the limit.

broader_coverage.reasoning: There is no ellipticity or self-adjointness requirement in the singular-value statement. The symbols of both one-sided Fourier multipliers are classical, with the leading terms zero for ξ<0; a smooth interpolation near ξ=0 makes no change at the integers.

evidence: Write z=exp(iθ), a_j=(1−jz)⁻¹ for j=s,t. The order −1 symbols of the extended operators are a_j/ξ for ξ>0 and zero for ξ<0. The scalar order −2 symbols commute. On ξ>0 the order −3 commutator symbol is (1/i) times the Poisson bracket: ξ⁻³ z a_t a_s(t a_t−s a_s)=(t−s)ξ⁻³ z a_t²a_s²; on ξ<0 it is zero.
The unit cosphere of the circle has directions ±1. Only the positive one contributes, so (2.9) is the cube of (2π)⁻¹∫|(t−s)z a_t²a_s²|^(1/3)dθ, precisely |t−s|J³.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The symbol calculation is direct in the known calculus, and the Schatten and harmonic-mean limits follow from that asymptotic.
